highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.221: Focus View Toggle Added to VS Code
highlights.summary: The latest release adds a Focus View mode to the VS Code extension that hides tool activity behind a collapsible per-turn summary, keeping your chat cleaner while still showing a live indicator when tools are running. Toggle it with Ctrl+Alt+F or via the Command Palette using 'Claude Code: Toggle Focus view'. This is especially useful if you find the tool call output overwhelming during long coding sessions.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Claude Opus 5 Now Default with 1M Context
highlights.summary: Claude Opus 5 is now available as the default Opus model in Claude Code, offering a massive 1 million token context window and a fast mode priced at $10/$50 per million tokens. This release also adds a strict network allowlist setting for sandboxed commands, giving you tighter control over what external hosts sandboxed tools can reach. If you work on large codebases, the 1M context window is a significant upgrade for whole-repo understanding.

highlights.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially announced Claude Opus 5, its most capable model yet, now integrated directly into Claude Code. The model is designed for complex, multi-step coding and reasoning tasks, making it a strong choice for developers tackling difficult engineering problems. Check the Anthropic blog for full details on capabilities, pricing, and how it compares to previous Opus versions.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218: /code-review Now Runs as a Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The /code-review slash command has been upgraded to run as a background subagent, meaning review work no longer floods your main conversation thread. This keeps your chat history clean and ensures stacked slash commands correctly target the code you intended to review. If you regularly use /code-review in your workflow, this change makes it significantly less disruptive.

highlights.title: How Does Claude Code Actually Work? Let's Make Our Own
highlights.summary: This YouTube video dives deep into the internals of Claude Code, explaining the architecture behind how it processes prompts, calls tools, and manages context. Building a simplified version from scratch is a great way to understand the system at a conceptual level, which helps you use it more effectively. Recommended for developers who want to go beyond surface-level usage and understand what's happening under the hood.

highlights.title: Claude Code Basics | Master 95% in 10 Minutes
highlights.summary: A concise YouTube tutorial that covers the most essential Claude Code features and workflows in just 10 minutes, making it ideal for developers just getting started. It focuses on the practical 20% of features that cover 95% of real-world use cases, so you can get productive fast. A great first video to watch before diving into longer or more advanced tutorials.

highlights.title: Show HN: Switch Claude Code Accounts Without Logging In Again
highlights.summary: A developer built a lightweight CLI tool called claude-account that lets you save multiple Claude Code accounts and switch between them instantly without going through the full login flow each time. Simple commands like 'claude account add myworkaccount' make it easy to separate work and personal usage. If you maintain multiple Claude accounts, this tool can save you significant friction every day.

highlights.title: 9-Minute Claude Code Setup Guide for China-Based Developers (Bilibili)
highlights.summary: This Bilibili video provides a beginner-friendly 9-minute walkthrough of installing and using Claude Code with a direct connection from mainland China, covering setup, core concepts, and real usage examples. It's particularly valuable for developers in regions where accessing Anthropic services directly can be challenging. The guide is concise and practical, promising no unnecessary filler.

tips_of_the_day: Use Focus View (Ctrl+Alt+F in VS Code) when you're in a long coding session to reduce visual noise — you'll still see a live indicator when tools are active, but your chat won't be buried under tool output.

Run /code-review as a background subagent by simply invoking it from a stacked slash command — since v2.1.218 it no longer pollutes your main conversation, so you can keep chatting while the review runs.

If you manage separate Claude Code accounts for work and personal projects, consider using a small account-switching CLI to avoid the full logout/login flow — saving even 2 minutes per switch adds up fast over a week.
